title: Felix and the Summer
premise: Tamsin Amberdale inherited Hollowmere Vineyard along with its crushing debts, and for ten years he has answered anonymous letters from a stranger who once saved his life in a courthouse corridor—letters he never answered in kind. When Felix Marsh, the letter-writer, buys the derelict cottage next door, Tamsin's carefully invisible life begins to unravel: the vineyard's debts trace back to the same man who destroyed Felix's family, and exposing him could save one of them and ruin the other. As harvest season ends and Felix's visa expires, Tamsin must choose between the loyalty that kept him silent and the truth that could keep Felix here—finally telling the letters what he never could, and letting someone stay after the last train leaves.
about_author: Cyrus Okonkwo is the pen name of a former paralegal who spent a decade watching people choose between justice and survival, and writes romances about the letters people never send. He lives near a failing vineyard he refuses to name, and answers every letter he receives.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. He walks the dying vineyard at dawn, tallying debts he can't pay and rereading a decade of unsigned letters he's never answered. Establishes his self-imposed invisibility and the quiet ritual that keeps him tethered. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as discipline.

chapters.title: The Man Who Bought the Cottage
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A moving van arrives at the derelict Hollis cottage; the new neighbor introduces himself as Felix Marsh, and Tamsin's blood runs cold—he recognizes the handwriting from the letters. Emotional beat: shock buried under forced politeness.

chapters.title: Borrowed Sugar, Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix settles in, openly delighted by the valley, and asks Tamsin endless small questions. We learn Felix came here deliberately, though he doesn't say why. Emotional beat: warmth Tamsin doesn't trust and can't refuse.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Tuesdays
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Flashback to the courthouse corridor where Felix, then a clerk, watched a terrified young Tamsin testify against his uncle—and began writing letters he never signed. Emotional beat: the origin of devotion and guilt entangled.

chapters.title: What the Vineyard Owes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A creditor arrives with paperwork Tamsin can't parse; the debts trace through shell companies to a name he buried years ago—his uncle Aldous Amberdale. Emotional beat: dread that the past has a paper trail.

chapters.title: Pruning Lessons
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix helps Tamsin prune the vines, and their hands keep meeting. Felix notices Tamsin flinches at questions about his family. Emotional beat: intimacy growing in the space where truth should be.

chapters.title: The Letter Tamsin Never Sent
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Alone, Tamsin finally drafts a reply to the letters, then burns it in the barrel behind the winery. He almost tells Felix about the correspondence and doesn't. Emotional beat: cowardice that feels like protection.

chapters.title: Aldous Amberdale's Shadow
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix, a former investigator, quietly pulls records on Aldous—the man whose fraud destroyed Felix's father and landed Felix's family in ruin. He doesn't yet connect Aldous to his gentle neighbor. Emotional beat: righteous anger sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The village festival forces them together publicly; a dance, too much wine, and a near-kiss interrupted by a creditor's call that makes Tamsin go pale. Emotional beat: joy interrupted by the ledger of the past.

chapters.title: The Name on the Deed
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix finds 'A. Amberdale' in the vineyard's old ownership papers and realizes his neighbor is the nephew of the man who ruined him. He says nothing, testing Tamsin instead. Emotional beat: betrayal he hasn't earned yet, bracing for it.

chapters.title: Confessions Over Bad Wine
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Drunk on failed vintage, Tamsin confesses everything except the letters: his testimony, his exile, his uncle's crimes. Felix listens and lies about who he is. Emotional beat: intimacy built on a mutual, asymmetric secret.

chapters.title: Visa Expiry
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix's right to remain runs out at season's end; his only path to staying is testimony that reopens the Amberdale case—testimony that would implicate Tamsin's family and the vineyard's title. Emotional beat: the clock becomes audible.

chapters.title: The Second Letter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin discovers a fresh letter in his mailbox—in Felix's handwriting, unposted, dated this week. The anonymous correspondent has a face and an address forty meters away. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past tense collapses.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Fence Line
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Tamsin accuses Felix of deception—ten years of letters, months of neighborly lies. Felix counters: Tamsin never answered once. Both retreat wounded. Emotional beat: the first real rupture.

chapters.title: Aldous Returns
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Aldous Amberdale arrives unannounced, out of prison early, demanding the vineyard be signed over to cover 'family obligations.' Tamsin realizes the debts were engineered to force exactly this. Emotional beat: the predator in the kitchen, familiar as weather.

chapters.title: What Felix Knows
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix has assembled the full fraud: Aldous looted the vineyard, framed Felix's father, and is now extorting Tamsin. Felix must choose—expose Aldous and destroy Tamsin's inheritance, or stay silent and lose his visa and his father's name. Emotional beat: the price of survival made concrete.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Aldous offers Tamsin a clean slate if he signs and stays silent; he mentions 'your little friend's immigration problem' with a smile. Tamsin, for the first time, says no. Emotional beat: the moment invisibility stops being an option.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. At an emergency hearing Felix files, both men testify—Felix to his father's framing, Tamsin against his uncle, their secrets laid bare in a room where loyalty and truth finally face each other. Emotional beat: exposure as liberation; holding hands under the table.

chapters.title: After the Verdict
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Aldous is remanded; the debts unravel as fraud, but the vineyard's fate hangs on an appeal Felix's testimony triggered. Felix's visa extension is granted provisionally—provisionally. Emotional beat: victory with an expiration date.

chapters.title: The Letters, Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix gives Tamsin the full box of ten years of letters, and Tamsin reads them aloud in the cellar, answering each one after a decade of silence. They finally speak the thing itself: love, named. Emotional beat: the past tense becomes present.

chapters.title: The Appeal
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The appellate ruling arrives: the vineyard's title is restored to Tamsin, but harvest is over and the vines are half-dead. Felix's permanent residency is approved the same afternoon. Emotional beat: grief and grace arriving together.

chapters.title: Letting Someone Stay
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, closing in Tamsin's. Spring pruning, two pairs of hands. The last train passes at dusk and neither of them is on it; Felix's suitcase is unpacked in the farmhouse. Tamsin writes a letter at last and hands it to Felix in person. Emotional beat: staying, chosen daily, as the answer to every unsent letter.
